statements.venue: Letter from Sen. Moreno to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei
statements.quote: We should not unnecessarily metastasize SI 'doomerism,' but rather recognize that SI, like any cutting-edge technology, presents risks that must be addressed by companies who are able to rise to the occasion.
statements.context: Moreno criticised Anthropic's leaders for warning publicly that advanced AI (which the letter calls super intelligence, 'SI') could kill everyone while the company prepares to sell shares to the public.
statements.source_label: Moreno letter to Dario Amodei (scanned PDF on moreno.senate.gov)
statements.reason: Labels warnings of catastrophic AI risk 'doomerism' and treats the risk as no different from that of any new technology, though it also says risks must be addressed.

statements.venue: Letter from Sen. Moreno to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei
statements.quote: Rather than highlighting how SI could end humanity, public discourse around SI should focus on developing solutions to the real vulnerabilities SI has found in American critical infrastructure and cybersecurity.
statements.context: Moreno argued that focus on catastrophic outcomes crowds out debate about national security and competition with China.
statements.source_label: Moreno letter to Dario Amodei (scanned PDF on moreno.senate.gov)
statements.reason: Says public discussion should stop highlighting the possibility that AI could end humanity and contrasts it with 'real' vulnerabilities, which sets the extinction concern aside without flatly denying it.

statements.venue: Letter from Sen. Moreno to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei
statements.quote: Anthropic's recent actions and statements reflect an alarmist approach to SI that places extraordinary emphasis on the technology's most catastrophic outcomes.
statements.context: Opening charge of the letter, before it cites statements by a former Anthropic researcher, an Anthropic safety researcher and Amodei about AI killing everyone.
statements.source_label: Moreno letter to Dario Amodei (scanned PDF on moreno.senate.gov)
statements.reason: Calls emphasis on catastrophic outcomes from AI alarmist.

statements.venue: Letter from Sen. Moreno to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei
statements.quote: We must address the risks associated with frontier SI. Doing so does not require halting its development or surrendering American technological dominance.
statements.context: Closing paragraph of the letter, on how the United States should respond to risks from advanced AI.
statements.source_label: Moreno letter to Dario Amodei (scanned PDF on moreno.senate.gov)
statements.reason: Read on its own, this says frontier AI carries risks that must be addressed, in general terms and without naming any catastrophic harm; it sits between C and D.

statements.venue: Remarks to the Daily Caller News Foundation
statements.quote: What [Trump] doesn't want is he doesn't want our AI industry destroyed because of irrational fears.
statements.context: Moreno was responding to President Trump's post opposing AI guardrails; the report says he added, "There are obviously concerns."
statements.reason: Calls fears about AI irrational, but the quote does not say which fears, so it is not certain he meant catastrophic risk.

statements.venue: Remarks to the Daily Caller News Foundation
statements.quote: He should, in fact, just shut down his entire company if he's so concerned about what he's creating.
statements.context: Moreno was asking why Anthropic's chief executive Dario Amodei is taking the company public if he is worried about the technology; the report has him adding, "The reality is that's an alarmist point of view."
statements.reason: Mocks Amodei's stated concern about the dangers of the AI his company builds and, in the next sentence, calls it alarmist.

slowdown.note: No statement found that addresses slowing AI progress as distinct from halting it; his remark that the President does not want the AI industry 'destroyed because of irrational fears' leans against, but does not name a slowdown.

pause.note: His own letter of 5 October 2026 says addressing the risks of frontier AI 'does not require halting its development'.
sources: Moreno letter to Dario Amodei, 5 October 2026

intl.note: Nothing found on an agreement or talks with China on AI; his letter only says the United States, not China, should shape the technology. News reports describe the September 2026 letter urging AI talks with China as signed by 17 Democratic senators, so Moreno, a Republican, was not a signer; no full signer list was seen.

rsi.note: Nothing found on a ban on self-improving AI.

record: Sent a letter on 5 October 2026 to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei criticising the company's 'alarmist approach' to advanced AI while it prepares a public share offering, and praising Amodei's signing of the White House Accord on Super Intelligence.
grade_reason: By the brief's rule the grade is the highest level found, and one sentence in his 5 October 2026 letter ('We must address the risks associated with frontier SI') is a borderline C. A reviewer should weigh that against five statements graded F, which are the main thrust of the letter and of his September remarks; if the borderline sentence is judged D, the grade becomes F.

The two Daily Caller quotes were returned by a page-fetching tool that summarises the page, which reported them as separate verbatim segments; I did not see the raw article text, the bracketed '[Trump]' is as reported from the article, and the article does not give the date of the remarks, so the article's date (15 September 2026) is used.
